items.title: Production Cell Simulator
items.technologies: Python 3 · JSON · CSV · Git · Visual Studio Code
highlights: Work orders, target quantities, signal intervals, and missed-signal conditions are configurable for each run.
Simulates detected and missed sensor signals, tracks produced pieces against the target, and stops when production is complete or the missed-signal limit triggers a sensor fault.
Writes timestamped events and a unique run ID to CSV; includes unit tests for signal handling, work-order outcomes, and fault conditions.

items.title: RunnerRPG
items.technologies: C# · Unity · Unity UI · ScriptableObjects · Adobe Illustrator · Adobe Photoshop · Inkscape
highlights: Built a personal Android RPG prototype in Unity and C# with turn-based battles, character skills and progression, inventory, and equipment upgrades.
Developed mobile screens for character menus, battle information, inventory, equipment, and progression; created original vector artwork for much of the interface.
Organized character, skill, and equipment data with ScriptableObjects and implemented local save and load; tested gameplay on an Android phone.

items.title: ESP8266 Weather Station and Binary Number Challenge
items.technologies: ESP8266 · C++ · Arduino · BME280 · SSD1306 OLED · I²C · Wi‑Fi

media.alt: ESP8266 prototype on a breadboard with an OLED showing the game-over score.
Demonstration of the connected weather station and binary number challenge.
Home page of the ESP8266 project's local web interface.
Wiring schematic for the ESP8266, SSD1306 OLED, and BME280.
Breadboard layout showing the ESP8266 project wiring.

highlights: Built a connected-object prototype with an ESP8266 and BME280 sensor to read temperature, humidity, pressure, and estimated altitude; displayed readings on an OLED and local web pages.
Added network time and a binary-number challenge in which three LEDs display values from 1 to 7; players select the matching decimal number with a button.
Implemented game feedback: correct answers increase the score, while a wrong answer ends the round and activates a buzzer.

items.title: Connected Weather Station with MicroPython Display and Zabbix
items.technologies: ESP8266 · C++ · Arduino · MicroPython · BME280 · SSD1306 OLED · Zabbix · JSON · Wi‑Fi

media.alt: Wiring diagram for the two ESP8266 boards, BME280 sensor, SSD1306 OLED, LEDs, buttons, and potentiometer.
Full demonstration of the connected weather station, MicroPython display, and Zabbix monitoring.

highlights: Connected two ESP8266 boards over a local network: one running Arduino/C++ reads BME280 data and controls two LEDs; the second runs MicroPython to display readings and LED states on an OLED.
Exposed sensor measurements and LED status through HTTP endpoints, with JSON data used by the display board.
Configured Zabbix to monitor the sensor readings and LED states.

items.title: IoT Sensor Monitoring with MQTT and Zabbix
items.technologies: ESP8266 · ESP32 · C++ · Arduino · MicroPython · BME280 · GY-521/MPU-6050 · SSD1306 OLED · MQTT · Mosquitto · Zabbix · HTTP/JSON · Wi‑Fi

media.alt: Conceptual system architecture showing microcontrollers, sensors, Mosquitto, Zabbix, and data flow.
Wiring diagram for the microcontroller boards and their sensors.
Demonstration of the IoT sensor monitoring system with MQTT and Zabbix.

highlights: Collected environmental measurements from a BME280 and motion and temperature readings from a GY-521/MPU-6050 sensor.
Published BME280 readings over MQTT using Mosquitto and exposed environmental and motion data through HTTP/JSON endpoints.
Configured Zabbix to monitor environmental measurements and selected motion-sensor values.

Organized files, tracked daily revenue, and scheduled recurring scripts with Crontab and Shell.
